ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, quadrilateral $ABCD$ is an inscribed quadrilateral of circle $\odot O$, the radius of $\odot O$ is 2, and $\angle B=135^\circ$. What is the measure of $\angle ADC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since quadrilateral $ABCD$ is inscribed in circle $O$, and $\angle B=135^\circ$,

$\therefore$ $\angle ADC=180^\circ-\angle B=45^\circ$,

thus $\angle ADC=\boxed{45^\circ}$

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, quadrilateral $ABCD$ is an inscribed quadrilateral of circle $\odot O$, the radius of $\odot O$ is 2, and $\angle B=135^\circ$. What is the measure of $\angle ADC$?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is a circle, points A, B, C, D are all on the circumference, and line segments AB, BC, CD, DA connect to form the cyclic quadrilateral ABCD; among them, vertex B and vertex D are a pair of opposite vertices of the quadrilateral, and ∠ADC is the angle at vertex D. Then reason: the opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary, so ∠B + ∠ADC = 180°. Given ∠B = 135°, therefore ∠ADC = 180° - 135° = 45°.
